name: MCP3221A4T-E_OT
title: 12-bit I2C A/D converter, low power, SOT-23
summary: The MCP3221 is a 12-bit successive-approximation ADC with one single-ended input, in a 5-pin SOT-23. It runs from one 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply that is also its reference, and talks over a two-wire I2C bus at 100 kHz or 400 kHz, reaching 22.3 ksps at 400 kHz. Conversion current is 250 µA maximum and standby 5 nA typical. Eight factory address options (A0 to A7) let up to eight share one bus.
key_figures: 2.7 V to 5.5 V, also the reference

notes: A5 (address bits 101) is the default option; other address options come from the factory.
Part number fields: MCP3221, address option A0 to A7, T for tape and reel, temperature E (-40°C to +125°C), package OT (SOT-23, 5-lead).

pins.name: VDD
pins.function: Supply, +2.7 V to 5.5 V. Also the full-scale reference of the converter.

pins.name: AIN
pins.function: Single-ended analog input into the sample-and-hold; converts correctly between VSS and VDD.

pins.name: SDA
pins.function: I2C serial data, in and out. Open drain: needs a pull-up to VDD, typically 10 kΩ at 100 kHz and 2 kΩ at 400 kHz. Changes only while SCL is low, except for Start and Stop.

pins.name: SCL
pins.function: I2C serial clock input that times data on SDA. Needs a pull-up to VDD, typically 10 kΩ at 100 kHz and 2 kΩ at 400 kHz.

circuits.title: Typical test configuration
circuits.description: VDD is 5 V, decoupled by 10 µF and 0.1 µF to ground. SDA and SCL each have a 2 kΩ pull-up to VDD. The input is a signal generator in series with a 2.5 V common-mode source, which returns to ground.

circuits.title: Pull-up resistors on the I2C bus
circuits.description: The converter on a two-wire bus with a PIC microcontroller as master. One pull-up from VDD on SDA and one on SCL; the analog signal goes straight into AIN. The pull-up value follows the bus speed: about 10 kΩ for 100 kHz, 2 kΩ for 400 kHz.

parts.note: 10 kΩ at fSCL = 100 kHz, 2 kΩ at fSCL = 400 kHz
10 kΩ at fSCL = 100 kHz, 2 kΩ at fSCL = 400 kHz

circuits.title: Powering the MCP3221
circuits.description: The recommended supply connection. VDD feeds the converter and is also its reference, so it is bypassed at the pin by 0.1 µF with 10 µF beside it to soak up higher-frequency noise on the rail. RPU pull-ups to VDD on SCL and SDA, which run on to the microcontroller.

circuits.title: Stable power and reference configuration
circuits.description: Because VDD is also the conversion reference, the converter is run from an MCP1541 4.096 V, 2% reference instead of the raw rail. The MCP1541 input has 0.1 µF to ground, its output carries a 1 µF load capacitor CL and feeds U1's VDD pin. The I2C pull-ups go to the system VDD, not to the reference.

operation.text: A successive-approximation converter: a capacitor array inside the part holds the input while a 12-bit SAR, DAC and comparator resolve it. Acquisition and conversion are timed by an on-chip clock, independent of SCL. Each finished result is held in a 12-bit register, readable whenever the master likes.
Conversion takes 8.96 µs typical, acquisition 1.12 µs typical; both follow the internal oscillator and not SCL.

Sample rate is one over the longest interval between successive acquisitions. For single conversions it is counted from one Start to the next, each conversion taking Start, address, both data bytes and Stop. In continuous mode the master acknowledges after each result and the next result follows after 18 clocks (two data bytes plus two acknowledge bits), which reaches 22.3 ksps at 400 kHz SCL.

The result is straight binary, MSB first, codes 0 to 4095. With no offset, gain or linearity error, AIN at or below VSS + 1/2 LSB reads 000h and AIN at or above VDD - 1.5 LSB reads FFFh. The first code transition ideally sits 1/2 LSB above VSS; the last 1.5 LSB below VDD.

DNL is each code's width minus the ideal 1 LSB after gain and offset are removed; positive means a wide code. INL is the cumulative deviation from a straight line, by the end-point method. Offset error is how far the first transition sits from its ideal place. Gain error is the last transition's distance from its ideal place, measured after offset is subtracted.

IDD is the average current over a 12-bit conversion. IDDA is the average current while the part watches the bus without being addressed. IDDS is the average current with no conversion running and SCL and SDA idle.

Transfers begin only from an idle bus, with SDA and SCL both high. SDA falling while SCL is high is Start; SDA rising while SCL is high is Stop. Data on SDA must be stable while SCL is high and change only while it is low, one clock per bit. The master sets the number of bytes between Start and Stop. The MCP3221 is always a slave; the master drives SCL and makes Start and Stop.

Every addressed receiver pulls SDA low through the ninth clock of each byte, which the master supplies. When reading, the master ends by leaving the last byte unacknowledged; the MCP3221 then lets go of SDA so the master can issue Stop.

The first byte after Start is the address: device code 1001, then address bits A2 A1 A0, then R/W. A2 to A0 are set at the factory per part number (A0 to A7 options; 101 is the default), so up to eight converters share one bus. Nothing in the part can be written, so a conversion needs R/W = 1.

Sampling begins as SCL falls at the end of the R/W bit; the internal clock then runs acquisition and conversion on its own. On the next rising edge the converter drives the acknowledge low, so the master must release SDA for that clock.

After acknowledging the address the part sends four zeros and D11 to D8. The master acknowledges low, then eight more clocks bring D7 to D0. The master answers that byte with a high (no acknowledge) to stop, and may then send Stop.

If the master acknowledges the lower data byte instead, the next sample begins as SCL falls on the LSB clock and two more data bytes follow, without a new address byte, for as long as the master keeps acknowledging. A Stop ends the sequence.
Sending the address with R/W = 0 makes the part acknowledge and release the bus without converting, which tells the master it is present. The master can then send Stop or a repeated Start.

Keep AIN between VSS and VDD. The source impedance adds to the 1 kΩ sampling switch and slows the charging of the 20 pF sample capacitor, so a high source impedance raises offset, gain and INL errors. A source near zero ohms is best; an op amp such as the MCP6022 gets there, its output impedance in closed loop being some tens of ohms.

SDA and SCL are open-drain and need pull-ups. How many devices share the bus is limited only by the 400 pF maximum bus capacitance; a bus may carry, for instance, a PIC16F876 master, a 24LC01 EEPROM, a TC74 temperature sensor and the MCP3221.

VDD is both supply and reference. Bypass it with 0.1 µF; a 10 µF in parallel helps where the rail carries higher-frequency noise. To power the part down after start-up, take VDD all the way to VSS: that ensures a full reset on the next power-up.

Fit the 0.1 µF bypass from VDD to ground as close to the pin as possible; it is always required. Keep digital and analog traces apart, run no traces under the part or its bypass capacitor, and keep clock and other fast lines well away from analog traces. An analog ground plane holds every device at one ground potential, and feeding VDD to each device in a star from one point cuts errors from shared return currents.
Where accuracy needs a steadier full scale than the rail gives, run VDD from a voltage reference; the MCP1541 4.096 V, 2% reference is the example.
